# PROCESS — cand_0002 (iteration 2/3)

## Environment faults (handed back, NOT edited for)
- 227-40, 45635: `rollout.error = "sandbox exec failed: 500 Server Error: Internal Server Error for url: http://127.0.0.1:34721/execute"`, `trace = None` (0 agent turns). 2/40 tasks. The sandbox execute endpoint returned HTTP 500 before the agent ran; a human must check the sandbox service on port 34721 (stability/restarts). No prompt edit made on their account.

## Ranked issue list
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | I. column-letter off-by-one from a positional header list | 43436 (1 trial, reward 0 → 1 recoverable) | Agent printed headers as a positional Python list (`['Record #', 'Department', ..., None, None, 'Department', 'Open as of today', 'Open by of end of May 2022', ...]`) and mapped them to letters by counting; it concluded "Column I: Open as of today (already filled)" — actually G=Department, H=Open as of today, I=May, J=Jun, K=Jul. It wrote the May/Jun counts into J/K, left I empty and never computed Jul. Its Phase 2 printout showed `I=None` for the column it believed "already filled" and it did not notice; then resent the same code 4×. | STRUCTURE (inspection output contract) + STRUCTURE (verify checklist item) | Phase 1 recipe prints address-keyed rows; prompt §3 bullet (knowledge: why counting slips); Phase 3 checklist item |
| — | ENV (sandbox 500) | 227-40, 45635 | infrastructure | ENV | none |

Semantics check (offline, from the trace's printed data): snapshot test `created<=b and (closed is None or closed>b)` gives May=[1,3,2,0,0], Jun=[2,4,2,0,0], Jul=[1,2,1,0,1]. The agent's written J/K values are exactly May/Jun shifted one column right → the snapshot rule (§2) was already right; the ONLY defect is the column mapping (6 wrong-value cells = shifted J/K, 5 empty = I). Feedback "6 cell(s) hold a different value of the right type; 5 cell(s) are empty" matches exactly.

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file | what | blast radius |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | Tighten output contract of the inspection step (ordered procedure) | task_template.md Phase 1 recipe | row printout now `[(cell.coordinate, value)]` for non-empty cells (cols capped at 30) + one sentence: take every column letter you write from this printout, by the header naming the quantity, never by counting preview headers | UNBOUNDED in form (recipe every task sees) but strictly more information; only 3/38 traces (31628, 560-12, 43436) even copied the `range(1, 12)` loop; the two passing ones get the same rows with letters attached |
| I | Add knowledge (why) | prompt.md §3 new bullet | multi-word headers / `Unnamed: k` make visual counts slip; positional lists hide letters; print row 1 keyed by coordinate | BOUNDED: only changes behavior when the agent derives a column letter |
| I | Pre-finish checklist item | task_template.md Phase 3 | each graded column's header names what you wrote; a column you thought "already filled" whose `was:` is `None` means letters are shifted → re-map | BOUNDED: fires only on that contradiction; passing tasks already map correctly |

Which file: the recipe & checklist live in task_template.md (where the agent copies code from); the reason lives in prompt.md §3 (preview-reading section). 

## Verify-the-fix
- trace 43436 turn 2 comment "Column I: Open as of today (already filled)" vs turn 3 output `Headers: ['Record #', 'Department', 'Date Created', 'Date Closed', None, None, 'Department', 'Open as of today', ...]` → with the new recipe the output would read `[("A1", "Record #"), ..., ("G1", "Department"), ("H1", "Open as of today"), ("I1", "Open by of end of May 2022"), ..., ("K1", "Open by end of Jul 2022")]`, so the letter for May is read, not counted → May→I, Jun→J, Jul→K; its own snapshot code then yields the expected values.
- trace 43436 turn 9 output `Row 2: I=None, J=1, K=2` (I believed pre-filled) → new Phase 3 item names exactly this contradiction as a "re-map columns" signal.
- Scorer check: feedback counts (6 shifted, 5 empty of 15) reproduce exactly under the shift hypothesis (computed offline above).
- Placeholders re-validated: `string.Formatter().parse` on the comment-stripped template → exactly the 7 allowed fields; `.format(...)` succeeds. The new recipe uses a list of `(coordinate, value)` tuples, deliberately with no literal braces.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single small cluster; CLAUDE.md forbids Agent/Workflow unless requested).
- Read prior_iterations/cand_0001 PROCESS + JOURNAL: 43436 was previously fixed by §2 snapshot rule + Phase 1b calibration; volatile. My edit does not touch those rules.

## Preserve
- §2 snapshot rule and Phase 1b calibration (they produced the right numbers in 43436).
- Everything listed in cand_0001's PRESERVE list.

## Deliberately skipped
- Duplicate-code resubmission loop in 43436 (4 identical blocks): already covered by Phase 3 text; the new checklist item gives it a concrete failing check to act on instead of adding emphasis.
- 80-42 append fix: passing now; no failing evidence this iteration.
- 227-40, 45635: environment.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
